claims.statement: `start_time` carries phenomenon time -- when the thing being described happened. Time series, windowing, and joins to other feeds are built on it.
claims.negative: Treating `start_time` as the time the record was produced, received, or published, or using a different member for event time.

claims.statement: Successive `start_time` values are expected at cadence `fixed` with period "PT30M". A cadence is an expectation and not a constraint: a record that departs from it is late, not invalid, and a missing value must not be filled in because the cadence says one was due.
claims.negative: Treating the cadence as a guarantee of completeness or as a validation rule, or interpolating absent values from it.

bare.note: Strongest is its principled refusal to compute per-member shares or a concentration index over a member set containing negatives; weakest is that it re-averages already-averaged values across a hopping window and presents thirteen output columns as five metrics.

prose.note: Strongest is converting the half-hourly means to MWh with the declared period length so the window sums are volumes rather than means of means; weakest is that those six-hour sums silently assume twelve periods are present while the completeness counter is explicitly left out.

annotated.note: Strongest is the explicit refusal to treat any mean as an instantaneous value or to synthesise a period end, with a spacing guard that nulls rather than fabricates a ramp; weakest is the LEFT JOIN between a per-event step and a windowed step, whose acceptance it cannot vouch for.

spec.note: Strongest is grounding every sum and every omission in the declared statistic, unit, supportPeriod and phenomenonTimeRelation rather than in fuel-name intuition; weakest is that refusing all cross-record aggregation leaves the selection thin, with a data-quality flag occupying one of the five slots.
